advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Replace the `_snapshot_schema.py`.exists() existence-only check with a behavioral assertion of the single-source-of-truth invariant (e.g. that the contract is loadable only via schemas.load and no second loadable snapshot-entry contract is registered).
evidence: The test body is a bare `.exists()` negation keyed to one hard-coded path string, with no assertion about the contract's shape or a duplicate-loading behavior.
The genuine anti-duplication guarantee is already carried by test_generated_typeddict_tracks_the_schema and the schemas.names() loader tests, which assert exactly-one loadable contract behaviorally.
advisory.finding: test_the_hand_rolled_module_no_longer_exists asserts only that a specific source path does not exist (a `test -f`-equivalent negative). It has no structural-contract purpose: it does not verify that a duplicate contract cannot be re-introduced under any name, and it would false-negative on a re-added duplicate with a different filename while false-positive-breaking on a benign relocation. This is an existence-only change-detector, not a behavior verifier.
scenarios: A future refactor that legitimately renames or moves the reconciler package breaks this test with no behavior change.
A regression that re-introduces a second hand-rolled contract under any other filename passes this test undetected.
advisory.suggested_fix: Drop the raw path `.exists()` assertion; rely on the loader/drift-gate tests that assert the contract is reachable exactly once through `schemas.names()` / `schemas.load`, which survive a package rename.
